attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; boundary refinement of claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention, claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast and claim.law.multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing - separates the SPELLING of a displacement constant from the TYPE/web changes those laws actually govern.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: The de-fakematch hazard laws (lwzu-idiom-web-retention, declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast, multifield-alias-defeats-indexed-addressing) all govern changes that alter a pointer's TYPE or introduce a typed intermediate lvalue. They do NOT govern merely re-SPELLING the displacement constant. Replacing a bare hex/decimal offset with a constant-folding named expression - `*(s32*)(e + 0x354)` -> `*(s32*)(e + offsetof(Enemy, route))`, or a pool-relative `*(s32*)(other + 3788)` -> `*(s32*)(other + (POOL_OFF + offsetof(Enemy, state)))` - keeps the base pointer's declared type, its web, and the single-additive-expression shape the front end sees, so the emitted instruction stream is bit-identical. Verified at scale in enemy.c: do_enemy_collide's 61 behavior-chain sites, explicitly recorded OFF-LIMITS by claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention because member conversion there splits the lwzu web, converted cleanly to offsetof form with the function staying at real 0 (MATCH); 99 e0-based sites across 15 move_logic functions and 75 shared flee-block sites likewise stayed byte-identical, including the exact worldmat[3][*] reads that had been PROVEN load-bearing minutes earlier (converting those same three sites to a typed `e->objgrp.worldmat[3][0]` member access broke move_logic05 from MATCH to 235/236 insns real 105). Consequence for de-fakematch campaigns: an 'off-limits' or 'left raw' region recorded under any web-retention law is only off-limits to TYPE conversion. The magic numbers in it can still be resolved to named fields via offsetof, recovering most of the documentation value at zero codegen risk. Do this pass FIRST across the whole TU - it is near-guaranteed neutral and needs only one gate - then attempt the riskier typed-member conversions on whatever remains. Caveat: the base pointer must genuinely point at the struct the offsetof names (verify the target displacements first), and the sum must remain ONE additive expression on the original pointer - do not introduce a typed intermediate, which re-enters the hazard laws.
